explanation: Traces of copper bind to a protein in the whites, making the foam more stable. Cooks without copper add a pinch of cream of tartar, an acid, for a similar effect.

claims.text: Whisking egg whites in a copper bowl makes the foam more stable, because copper ions bind to the egg-white protein conalbumin (ovotransferrin).
Aluminium, stainless steel and cast iron bowls do not stabilize egg-white foam in the way copper does.
Cream of tartar, an acid, is added to egg whites to stabilize the foam, with an effect similar to a copper bowl's.

evidence.restatement: Copper ions from a copper bowl bind to conalbumin (ovotransferrin) in egg white, making the foam more stable.
Stainless steel, aluminium and cast-iron bowls do not stabilize egg-white foam the way copper does.
Cream of tartar, an acid, is added to egg whites to stabilize the foam, much as a copper bowl does.
Harold McGee: copper ions from the bowl bind the egg-white protein conalbumin (ovotransferrin) and make the foam more stable.
Aluminium, stainless steel and cast iron release no ions that bind conalbumin; stainless steel is neutral and aluminium can grey the foam.

claimResults.note: Tested stainless steel as a second answer: it is a fine bowl but gives no stabilising effect.

evidence.restatement: An acid such as cream of tartar stabilises egg-white foam, an alternative to copper.

stem: Whisking egg whites in a bowl made of which metal helps the foam hold its shape?
